title: POC scope: hosting decision framework - Concordia Insurance
summary: Initial POC scoping to choose hosting mode (hosted / dedicated / private). Discussed success criteria (latency, availability, cost), workload sizing (peak RPS, token distribution), benchmark plan and 6-week pilot timeline. Security and data residency flagged as blockers for private path. Agreed next steps: benchmark spreadsheet, security checklist, pricing comparison, schedule bench run week 2.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark plan and cost model (Maya) - by 2025-06-05
Customer to provide 7-day traffic sample and sample prompts (Rajiv) - by 2025-06-06
Security to review SOC2/KMS notes and reply (Monica) - by 2025-06-09
Schedule benchmark run and kick off pilot week of 2025-06-16

Evan Chen — prepare initial perf test harness and instructions for traffic replay (due 2025-06-06)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Participants: Maya (Redwood AE), Evan (Redwood SE), Laura (Concordia Head of Data), Rajiv (Platform), Monica (Security), Tom (Product)

Summary notes: see summary section above

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick agenda — align on success criteria, sizing, and pick a hosting path so we can scope the POC.
00:18 Laura: thanks, Maya. we, um, want to validate latency and cost — like we need this to be predictable for policy-document generation. our users expect near realtime.
00:30 Rajiv: by realtime she means like sub-300ms p95 ideally, but that's for short prompts. for longer doc generation maybe 500–700ms is fine if throughput holds.
00:45 Evan: okay, good. couple clarifying q's — what's your expected QPS during peak? and token lengths?
00:52 Laura: peak is around 120 rps right now for the pilot scope, bursts to 200 for a couple of minutes. average token length about 350 tokens per request, but we have a long tail up to 1,200 tokens.
01:10 Tom: and just to flag, product wants <250ms p95 on the 80% of requests that are short templates, the longer ones can be SL lower priority.
01:25 Maya: perfect. that's helpful. so for decision framing: Hosted (our Redwood API) gives fastest onboarding and no infra ops; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput and we can set SLOs; Private/VPC gives full control and on-prem options for compliance but longer lead time and lift.
01:46 Monica: on compliance — Concordia requires audit trails, KMS control, and data residency in eu-west for european customers. SOC2 is a must. can Redwood support customer-managed keys?
01:56 Evan: yes — for Private we support customer KMS/HSM. for Dedicated we can integrate with cloud KMS and godeep peering; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption but not customer-managed HSM in the initial tier. there was a small pause — sorry, envelope is our standard, customer-managed keys are available on Dedicated and Private.
02:20 Rajiv: network egress is also a concern. if we use Hosted, egress costs add up and peering options are limited — can you share numbers for expected egress?
02:33 Maya: yep we'll include a rough egress estimate in the cost worksheet. that'll show modeled monthly spend for your 120–200rps profile.
02:40 Laura: one more — fallback behavior. we need automatic fallback to a cheaper model for degraded latency. do you have that?
02:49 Evan: yeah, we have routing policies and automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants — it's built into the serving plane. sometimes the transcription in our system comes out as 'routing polices' but it's routing policies, sorry.
03:05 Tom: for benchmarks, can we run a replay of our 24–72h traffic and compare three configs: Hosted (prod-like), Dedicated (provisioned GPUs), Private (small on-prem cluster)?
03:16 Evan: yes. typical plan is: replay traffic with representative prompts, measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per token, GPU utilization, and memory/KV cache hit rates. we'll also measure cold start behavior and tail latency.
03:32 Rajiv: cold start matters — our burst pattern is short but sharp. if Dedicated can keep warm pools and autoscale quickly that's a pro.
03:41 Evan: Dedicated supports pre-warmed pools and burst capacity; we'll include warm-up experiments.
03:48 Laura: what's the expected timeline for the POC? product wants a working demo in 6–8 weeks.
03:55 Maya: we typically run a 6-week pilot: week 1 - onboarding + data sample collection + bench plan finalization; week 2 - run baseline Hosted benchmark; week 3 - spin up Dedicated env and run bench; week 4 - run private/on-prem bench (if chosen) and iterate; week 5 - quality evaluation + regressions; week 6 - run final acceptance tests and handoff. if private needs procurement it can add 2–4 weeks.
04:18 Monica: procurement on our side is slow — might take extra time for VPC peering and HSM approvals. that likely pushes Private out unless the business requires it.
04:30 Rajiv: in terms of cost, can you show us cost per 1M tokens across each mode and a sensitivity to batch size and quantization?
04:40 Maya: yes — we'll include cost models with different quantization profiles and batching assumptions. quick note: quantized models can reduce GPU memory and cost but sometimes impact quality — we should add a quality regression check to the benchmark.
04:55 Tom: can Redwood measure generation perplexity or QA-based scoring versus your baseline?
05:02 Evan: we can run evals against a golden set and provide pass/fail thresholds plus a small human spot-check sample; recommend automated BLEU-like or ROUGE-like metrics plus domain-specific checks. those are noisy but useful.
05:20 Laura: ok, security gating — Monica, what's the minimum to even consider Hosted?
05:26 Monica: Hosted acceptable if envelope encryption and SOC2 plus contractual clauses for data residency in the eu. if any PHI or regulated PII goes through the system we need KMS and dedicated tenancy.
05:38 Maya: noted. we'll surface options: Hosted with contractual controls, Dedicated with cloud KMS and VPC peering, Private with full KMS/HSM and on-prem.
05:50 Rajiv: what's the rollback/incident model? we need tracing and token-level cost attribution, plus audit logs for every request.
06:00 Evan: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency, distributed traces, and audit logs — we can provide log-forwarding to your SIEM and long-term retention as an addon. there might be a small transcription error earlier where 'trace hooks' got recorded as 'trace books' in our notes.
06:20 Tom: ok great. can you put together a minimal acceptance criteria doc — e.g., p95 < 250ms for short templates, throughput >= 100 rps sustained, cost target <$X per 1M tokens, quality delta within 3% of baseline?
06:34 Maya: yes we'll draft acceptance criteria and put numbers into the benchmark template.
06:40 Laura: about dataset — we'll supply sample prompts and a redacted dataset. Rajiv will deliver a traffic dump.
06:48 Rajiv: yep — i'll anonymize and upload to the shared S3 you provided in the onboarding notes.
06:55 Maya: excellent. next steps recap: we share benchmark plan and cost model by 2025-06-05; customer shares traces by 2025-06-06; security confirms gating items by 2025-06-09; schedule bench run week of 2025-06-16.
07:10 Monica: sounds good. also please include a short checklist for the security team — we need KMS flow, key rotation, SSO/SAML integration points, and audit log retention options.
07:22 Evan: got it. we'll include an appendix with SSO/SAML and RBAC details and the supported logging endpoints.
07:28 Laura: one small ask — can you show the degradation behavior in the benchmark if a zone fails and traffic routes to fallback model? we need that resiliency story.
07:37 Evan: yes, we'll include a chaos-style test: simulate region outage and measure failover latency and success rate.
07:44 Tom: any blockers from Redwood side to start week of 2025-06-16?
07:49 Maya: no blockers, as long as we get the trace and security requirements. depending on procurement we may postpone Private bench. but Dedicated and Hosted benchmarks are go.
07:59 Rajiv: ok i'll get the data in the next 4 days.
08:03 Maya: awesome. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and a calendar invite for the bench kick-off.
08:10 Laura: thanks all, bye.
08:12 Monica: thanks, bye.

Notes on transcript imperfections: occasional mis-hears (e.g., 'KV cash' vs KV cache), small punctuation issues, generic speaker labels used in some segments, occasional run-on sentences from customer side.
